projects.title: StreamFair
projects.description: - StreamFair is built in 24 hours which is a browser extension + backend system that introduces per-second streaming payments for video content using RLUSD (Ripple's USD stablecoin) on the XRP Ledger.- Instead of subscriptions, viewers pay micro-amounts in real-time as they watch. Close the video halfway? You paid for half. - The price itself is shaped by community engagement. If most people watch only 30% of a video, the price adjusts to reflect that.

projects.title: Armie
projects.description: - ARMIE is a mixed-reality surgical training system built in 48 hours that allows students to practice procedures safely, affordably, and repeatedly.- Students operate a real robotic arm while visualizing a virtual patient through AR. All movements are captured, logged, and compared against expert demonstrations.- ARMIE is designed to augment, not replace, cadaveric training.- It provides a pre-clinical simulation layer that enables repetition, standardization, and objective skill measurement before live tissue exposure.

projects.title: Feel-IT
projects.description: - Feel-IT is built in 36 hours- Millions of deaf or hard-of-hearing people miss critical audio cues like alarms, knocks, or cries — Feel-IT turns these sounds into clear, recognizable vibrations- Using Apple’s SoundAnalysis, the iPhone identifies over 100 environmental sounds and only alerts the user for the specific ones they choose, preventing sensory overload- The ESP32 wearable displays the detected sound label and triggers a precise DRV2605L-powered “Triple Click” vibration within a second, giving users immediate awareness of their surroundings

stacked 2 wins at LA Hacks . won overall track of catalyst for change and company track of Fetch.ai . we built dots. an app that helps businesses make their spaces accessible to blind people at a fraction of today's cost. a tactile braille map and an ai voice agent at every room entrance. before stepping in, you know exactly what's inside. my cousin brother karan is visually impaired. we interviewed him before writing a single line of code. he walked us through the daily friction of navigating spaces and served as a massive inspiration for the project. sharing the win with him on facetime broke me in the best way. his reaction made the 36 hours worth it ten times over. would like to thank Sana Wajid , Devam Sheth , Rajashekar V , Martin Angel Ceballos for their support throughout the hackathon. had an absolute honor to present this idea to incredible judges like Megha Manglani , Baba J. , Vartul Agrawal , Sanket Gautam , Parth Chandak , and more. check out our demo here - https://lnkd.in/gesrY3UA ...more

A special thank you to Professor Jenny T.Y. Ling of Tamkang University for inviting me to join Nomad Studio, an architectural exchange program in New York, and to deliver a lecture on XR and demonstrate a OXR at Columbia University GSAPP. It was a pleasure to introduce OXR to architecture students and share its spatial presentation and orchestration capabilities with faculty from New York Institute of Technology ( Evan Shieh )and Parsons School of Design - The New School ( Hyon Woo Scott Chung ). I was also grateful for the opportunity to meet members of the GSAPP leadership, including its dean and associate dean. During the exchange, I shared how my architectural education laid the foundation for my journey into human-computer interaction, mixed reality, and entrepreneurship. I also spoke with the students about moving to the United States, building OXR, and eventually securing investment from U.S. venture capital firms. Architecture opens doors far beyond the traditional path of becoming an architect. I encouraged the students to explore broadly and discover how architectural thinking can contribute to technology, research, entrepreneurship, and many other fields. I especially appreciate Professor Lin for organizing Nomad Studio and giving students the opportunity to develop an international perspective at such an early stage in their education. I am grateful for everyone’s encouragement and look forward to exploring future collaborations.

I’m delighted to have graduated with a First-Class BSc (Hons) in Computer Science with Artificial Intelligence from the University of Nottingham last week! This happened right after a busy weekend in San Francisco at the Y Combinator Startup School, where I got to see leaders in tech such as Jensen Huang , Sam Altman, Garry Tan , and Boris Cherny , to name a few, give really interesting talks regarding frontier models, the latest harnesses, and industry adoption, along with a lot of free AI credits. Excited to return to Goldman Sachs full-time on the Electronic Trading Platforms team, where I will be working on high-performance compute infra for trading systems, FPGA development, and monitoring.

Recently, I had the opportunity to present my research poster, “Real-Time Image-Guided Focus Control in Optical Coherence Tomography,” at the 2026 Summer Undergraduate Research Symposium. This experience was a meaningful conclusion to my SURE internship and allowed me to share my work on liquid-lens focus control, OCT imaging, and image processing. I am very grateful to Dr. Jenny (Jungeun) Won for being a great mentor throughout this project and to Dr. Cecilia Martínez León for leading and supporting our SURE cohort. #UndergraduateResearch #SURE #OpticalCoherenceTomography #BiomedicalImaging #ImageProcessing #UniversityAtBuffalo
